claim: GnRH neurons exhibit pulse and surge modes of activity to control fertility.
source: The gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons exhibit pulse and surge modes of activity to control fertility.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact about GnRH neurons.

claim: GnRH neurons exhibit an unusual bipolar morphology comprised of a classical soma-proximal dendritic zone and an elongated secretory process that can operate as both a dendrite and an axon, termed a 'dendron'.
source: They also exhibit an unusual bipolar morphology comprised of a classical soma-proximal dendritic zone and an elongated secretory process that can operate as both a dendrite and an axon, termed a 'dendron'.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known characteristic of GnRH neurons.

claim: The highest density of synaptic inputs to a GnRH neuron exists at its distal dendron.
source: We show using expansion microscopy that the highest density of synaptic inputs to a GnRH neuron exists at its distal dendron.
evidence: This claim is supported by expansion microscopy data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Selective chemogenetic inhibition of the GnRH neuron distal dendron abolishes the luteinizing hormone (LH) surge.
source: In vivo, selective chemogenetic inhibition of the GnRH neuron distal dendron abolishes the luteinizing hormone (LH) surge and markedly dampens LH pulses.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from chemogenetic inhibition experiments.

claim: Selective chemogenetic inhibition of the GnRH neuron distal dendron markedly dampens LH pulses.
source: In vivo, selective chemogenetic inhibition of the GnRH neuron distal dendron abolishes the luteinizing hormone (LH) surge and markedly dampens LH pulses.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from chemogenetic inhibition experiments.

claim: Inhibitory chemogenetic and optogenetic strategies targeting the GnRH neuron soma-proximal dendritic zone abolish the LH surge.
source: In contrast, inhibitory chemogenetic and optogenetic strategies targeting the GnRH neuron soma-proximal dendritic zone abolish the LH surge but have no effect upon LH pulsatility.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from chemogenetic and optogenetic inhibition experiments.

claim: Inhibitory chemogenetic and optogenetic strategies targeting the GnRH neuron soma-proximal dendritic zone have no effect upon LH pulsatility.
source: In contrast, inhibitory chemogenetic and optogenetic strategies targeting the GnRH neuron soma-proximal dendritic zone abolish the LH surge but have no effect upon LH pulsatility.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from chemogenetic and optogenetic inhibition experiments.

claim: Electrical activity at the soma-proximal dendrites of the GnRH neuron is only essential for the LH surge.
source: These observations indicate that electrical activity at the soma-proximal dendrites of the GnRH neuron is only essential for the LH surge while the distal dendron represents an autonomous zone where synaptic integration drives pulsatile GnRH secretion.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The distal dendron represents an autonomous zone where synaptic integration drives pulsatile GnRH secretion.
source: These observations indicate that electrical activity at the soma-proximal dendrites of the GnRH neuron is only essential for the LH surge while the distal dendron represents an autonomous zone where synaptic integration drives pulsatile GnRH secretion.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In females, GnRH neurons secrete GnRH into the pituitary portal circulation either as discrete pulses approximately once every hour or as a prolonged surge at the mid-point of the ovarian cycle to initiate ovulation.
source: In females, these neurons secrete GnRH into the pituitary portal circulation either as discrete pulses approximately once every hour or as a prolonged surge at the mid-point of the ovarian cycle to initiate ovulation (Goodman, 2015; Karsch et al., 1997; Levine, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: GnRH neurons exhibit a bipolar morphology with synaptic inputs clustered around the soma and proximal dendrites.
source: The GnRH neurons exhibit a bipolar morphology with synaptic inputs clustered around the soma and proximal dendrites (Campbell et al., 2005; Li et al., 2016; Moore et al., 2015) and the action potential initiation site located 50–100 μm down one of the dendritic processes (Herde and Herbison, 2015; Iremonger and Herbison, 2012; Roberts et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The action potential initiation site in GnRH neurons is located 50–100 μm down one of the dendritic processes.
source: The GnRH neurons exhibit a bipolar morphology with synaptic inputs clustered around the soma and proximal dendrites (Campbell et al., 2005; Li et al., 2016; Moore et al., 2015) and the action potential initiation site located 50–100 μm down one of the dendritic processes (Herde and Herbison, 2015; Iremonger and Herbison, 2012; Roberts et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: One or both of the dendritic processes arising from a GnRH neuron can project for over 4000 μm before terminating in short neurosecretory axons within the secretory zone of the median eminence.
source: However, recent studies in the mouse have highlighted that one or both of the dendritic processes arising from a GnRH neuron can project for over 4000 μm before terminating in short neurosecretory axons within the secretory zone of the median eminence (Herde et al., 2013; Moore et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: GnRH neuron processes conduct action potentials from the soma-dendritic zone but also receive synaptic inputs.
source: Unusually, these processes conduct action potentials from the soma-dendritic zone but also receive synaptic inputs, with their blended dendritic/axonal properties leading them to be termed 'dendrons' (Herde et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The density of synaptophysin-immunoreactive elements forming synaptic appositions along the first 60 μm of the primary dendrite (soma-dendritic zone) was 0.8 ± 0.3 synapses/10 μm membrane.
source: The density of synaptophysin-immunoreactive elements forming synaptic appositions along the first 60 μm (252 μm post-expansion) of the primary dendrite (soma-dendritic zone) was 0.8 ± 0.3 synapses/10 μm membrane with 95% of dendrites (N = 4 female mice) exhibiting synapses (Figure 1A–C, Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by expansion microscopy data and quantitative analysis presented in Table 1 and Figure 1.

claim: 95% of soma-dendritic zone dendrites exhibited synapses.
source: The density of synaptophysin-immunoreactive elements forming synaptic appositions along the first 60 μm (252 μm post-expansion) of the primary dendrite (soma-dendritic zone) was 0.8 ± 0.3 synapses/10 μm membrane with 95% of dendrites (N = 4 female mice) exhibiting synapses (Figure 1A–C, Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by expansion microscopy data and quantitative analysis presented in Table 1 and Figure 1.

claim: The synaptic density at the level of the distal dendron was 2.0 ± 0.2 synapses/10 μm.
source: The same analysis at the level of the distal dendron found 2.0 ± 0.2 synapses/10 μm with 53% of dendritic elements having at least one synapse along the 15 μm (63 μm post-expansion) segment analysed (N = 4) (Figure 1D–F, Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by expansion microscopy data and quantitative analysis presented in Table 1 and Figure 1.

claim: 53% of distal dendron dendritic elements had at least one synapse along the 15 μm segment analysed.
source: The same analysis at the level of the distal dendron found 2.0 ± 0.2 synapses/10 μm with 53% of dendritic elements having at least one synapse along the 15 μm (63 μm post-expansion) segment analysed (N = 4) (Figure 1D–F, Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by expansion microscopy data and quantitative analysis presented in Table 1 and Figure 1.

claim: There is a 2.5-fold higher density of synaptic inputs onto GnRH neuron distal dendrons compared to their soma-dendritic zone.
source: These observations indicate a 2.5-fold higher density of synaptic inputs onto GnRH neuron distal dendrons compared to their soma-dendritic zone suggesting a physiologically important role.
evidence: This is calculated from the synaptic density data presented in the manuscript.

claim: 64 ± 2.6% of rPOA GnRH neurons expressed hM4Di-mCherry following AAV injection into the ME.
source: Dual label immunohistochemistry showed that 64 ± 2.6% of rPOA GnRH neurons expressed hM4Di-mCherry (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D) (N = 6).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data presented in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: ~70% of rPOA GnRH neurons are hypophysiotropic.
source: Prior estimates indicate that ~70% of rPOA GnRH neurons are hypophysiotropic (Campos and Herbison, 2014; Merchenthaler et al., 1989).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A LH surge commenced between 17:00 and 18:00 hr in OVX+E+P wild-type and GnRH-Cre mice.
source: Initial studies using hourly tail-tip bleeding in OVX+E+P wild-type and GnRH-Cre mice that had not received AAV injections demonstrated that a LH surge commenced between 17:00 and 18:00 hr (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: An LH surge occurred in all saline-treated wild-type OVX+E+P mice (N = 9).
source: Whereas an LH surge occurred in all saline- (N = 9) and CNO- (N = 11) treated wild-type mice (Figure 2C,D,G), as well as saline-treated GnRH-Cre mice (N = 12)(Figure 2E,G), the LH surge was abolished in CNO-treated GnRH-Cre mice (N = 11)(Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2C, D, and G.

claim: An LH surge occurred in all CNO-treated wild-type OVX+E+P mice (N = 11).
source: Whereas an LH surge occurred in all saline- (N = 9) and CNO- (N = 11) treated wild-type mice (Figure 2C,D,G), as well as saline-treated GnRH-Cre mice (N = 12)(Figure 2E,G), the LH surge was abolished in CNO-treated GnRH-Cre mice (N = 11)(Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2C, D, and G.

claim: An LH surge occurred in all saline-treated GnRH-Cre OVX+E+P mice (N = 12).
source: Whereas an LH surge occurred in all saline- (N = 9) and CNO- (N = 11) treated wild-type mice (Figure 2C,D,G), as well as saline-treated GnRH-Cre mice (N = 12)(Figure 2E,G), the LH surge was abolished in CNO-treated GnRH-Cre mice (N = 11)(Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2E and G.

claim: The LH surge was abolished in CNO-treated GnRH-Cre OVX+E+P mice (N = 11) following global GnRH neuron inhibition.
source: Whereas an LH surge occurred in all saline- (N = 9) and CNO- (N = 11) treated wild-type mice (Figure 2C,D,G), as well as saline-treated GnRH-Cre mice (N = 12)(Figure 2E,G), the LH surge was abolished in CNO-treated GnRH-Cre mice (N = 11)(Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2F and G.

claim: LH levels were significantly reduced at 19:00 (p<0.001) and 20:00 (p<0.05) time points in CNO-treated GnRH-Cre OVX+E+P mice compared to controls.
source: Mean LH levels in all three surging groups (Figure 2G) were the same as those observed in mice that had not received AAV injections (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), while LH levels were significantly reduced at both 19:00 (p<0.001, two-way repeated ANOVA) and 20:00 time points in CNO-treated GnRH-Cre mice (p<0.05, two-way repeated ANOVA) (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data presented in Figure 2G.

claim: Saline-treated OVX GnRH-Cre mice exhibited a normal pulsatile pattern of LH release with ~3 ng/ml amplitude pulses occurring every ~15 min (N = 6).
source: Mice treated with saline exhibited a normal pulsatile pattern of LH release with ~3 ng/ml amplitude pulses occurring every ~15 min (N = 6)(Figure 2H,I,L,M).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2H, I, L, and M.

claim: CNO-treated OVX GnRH-Cre mice exhibited significantly fewer and small amplitude (~0.5 ng/ml) LH pulses (N = 6, p<0.001) compared to saline controls.
source: In contrast, mice treated with CNO exhibited much reduced LH levels with significantly fewer and small amplitude (~0.5 ng/ml) LH pulses (N = 6)(p<0.001,Mann-Whitney test)(Figure 2J–M).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis presented in Figure 2J-M.

claim: Mean levels of LH were 2.7 ng/ml in saline-treated OVX GnRH-Cre mice and 0.8 ng/ml (p<0.001) in CNO-treated mice.
source: Mean levels of LH were 2.7 ng/ml in saline and 0.8 ng/ml (p<0.001, Mann-Whitney test) in CNO-treated mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis presented in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Injection of CNO into the MBH of AAV-injected OVX+E+P GnRH-Cre mice (N = 12) abolished the LH surge in all mice.
source: Injection of saline into the MBH of AAV-injected OVX+E+P GnRH-Cre mice (N = 12) had no effect on the occurrence of the LH surge (Figure 3C,E), whereas injection of CNO (N = 12) abolished the LH surge in all mice (Figure 3D,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 3D and E.

claim: LH levels were significantly reduced at 19:00, 20:00 and 21:00 time points in CNO-treated GnRH-Cre OVX+E+P mice following MBH injection (p<0.001).
source: LH levels were significantly reduced at 19:00, 20:00 and 21:00 time points in CNO-treated GnRH-Cre mice (p<0.001, two-way repeated ANOVA) (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data presented in Figure 3E.

claim: MBH injection of CNO in AAV-injected OVX GnRH-Cre mice resulted in a substantial reduction in both the amplitude (p<0.001) and frequency (p<0.05) of LH pulses compared to saline controls.
source: The same strategy employed in AAV-injected OVX GnRH-Cre mice resulted in normal LH pulsatility in saline-treated animals (N = 8)(Figure 3F,G), but a substantial reduction in both the amplitude (p<0.001, Mann-Whitney test) and frequency (p<0.05, Mann-Whitney test) of LH pulses in mice receiving CNO (N = 7)(Figure 3H–K).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis presented in Figure 3H-K.

claim: Mean levels of LH were 3.2 ng/ml in saline-treated and 0.7 ng/ml (p<0.001) in CNO-treated OVX GnRH-Cre mice following MBH injection.
source: Mean levels of LH were 3.2 ng/ml in saline and 0.7 ng/ml (p<0.001, Mann-Whitney test) in CNO-treated mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis presented in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D,E.

claim: An LH surge occurred in all saline-treated GnRH-Cre OVX+E+P mice (N = 9) following rPOA injection.
source: Although an LH surge occurred in all saline-treated mice (N = 9)(Figure 4B), this was abolished in mice receiving CNO into the rPOA (N = 10)(Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4B.

claim: The LH surge was abolished in mice receiving CNO into the rPOA (N = 10).
source: Although an LH surge occurred in all saline-treated mice (N = 9)(Figure 4B), this was abolished in mice receiving CNO into the rPOA (N = 10)(Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4C and D.

claim: LH levels were significantly reduced at 19:00, 20:00 and 21:00 time points in CNO-treated GnRH-Cre OVX+E+P mice following rPOA injection (p<0.001).
source: The levels of LH were significantly reduced at 19:00, 20:00 and 21:00 time points in CNO-treated GnRH-Cre mice (p<0.001, two-way repeated ANOVA) (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data presented in Figure 4D.

claim: Injection of CNO into the rPOA of AAV-injected OVX GnRH-Cre mice had no effect upon pulsatile LH secretion.
source: For pulsatile LH secretion, the same injection of saline (N = 8) or CNO (N = 9) into the rPOA of AAV-injected OVX mice 10 min prior to blood sampling was found to have no effect upon pulsatile LH secretion with no differences detected in LH profiles (Figure 4E–H), mean pulse amplitude (Figure 4I), frequency (Figure 4J) or mean LH levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4E-J and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F,G.

claim: 96±2% GnRH cell bodies expressed GFP in GnRH-Cre+/-;FLEX-Rosa-CAG-Arch-GFP+/+ mice.
source: Archaerhodopsin-3 was expressed selectively in GnRH neurons by crossing GnRH-Cre and FLEX-Rosa-CAG-Arch-GFP+/+ mouse lines resulting in 96±2% GnRH cell bodies expressing GFP (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A) with extension into the long projections to the ME.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data presented in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Short periods (1–10 s) of yellow light (593 nm) illumination hyperpolarized and effectively silenced GnRH neuron firing in brain slices.
source: Brain slice electrophysiological studies in these mice demonstrated that short periods (1–10 s) of yellow light (593 nm) illumination hyperpolarized and effectively silenced GnRH neuron firing (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Continuous illumination for periods of minutes significantly reduced firing but showed variable efficacy in GnRH neurons.
source: Continuous illumination for periods of minutes also significantly reduced firing but showed variable efficacy (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E,F), while a 10 s on 10 s off pattern of light illumination remained effective in suppressing firing during illumination for minutes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: A 10 s on 10 s off pattern of light illumination remained effective in suppressing firing during illumination for minutes in GnRH neurons.
source: Continuous illumination for periods of minutes also significantly reduced firing but showed variable efficacy (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E,F), while a 10 s on 10 s off pattern of light illumination remained effective in suppressing firing during illumination for minutes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The LH surge was abolished completely with bilateral yellow light illumination of the rPOA in GnRH-Cre+/-;FLEX-Rosa-CAG-Arch-GFP+/+ mice (N = 12).
source: In contrast, the LH surge was abolished completely with bilateral yellow light illumination of the rPOA (N = 12)(Figure 5D,F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 5D and F.

claim: Bilateral 593 nm yellow light illumination of the rPOA for 40 min had no effect on pulsatile LH secretion in OVX GnRH-Cre+/-;FLEX-Rosa-CAG-Arch-GFP+/+ mice.
source: Three-minute tail tip blood samples were taken from OVX GnRH-Cre+/-;FLEX-Rosa-CAG-Arch-GFP+/+ mice for 2 hr with bilateral 593 nm yellow light illumination of the rPOA occurring from 40 to 80 min. This was found to have no effect on pulsatile LH secretion (Figure 5G,H) with pulse amplitude (Figure 5I), frequency (Figure 5J) and mean LH levels (Figure 5O) remaining unchanged during the illumination period.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 5G-J and O.

claim: CNO administered to wild-type mice has no impact upon pulsatile LH secretion.
source: We have previously reported that CNO administered to wild-type mice has no impact upon pulsatile LH secretion (Coutinho et al., 2020) and demonstrate here that, equally, CNO has no impact on the LH surge in wild-type mice.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and experimental data in the current manuscript.

claim: CNO has no impact on the LH surge in wild-type mice.
source: We have previously reported that CNO administered to wild-type mice has no impact upon pulsatile LH secretion (Coutinho et al., 2020) and demonstrate here that, equally, CNO has no impact on the LH surge in wild-type mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in the current manuscript.

claim: The activating yellow light has no impact on LH pulses or the LH surge in wild-type mice.
source: We have also performed both yellow and blue light laser controls in these studies and show that the activating yellow light has no impact on LH pulses or the LH surge in wild-type mice and that switching to the incorrect wavelength blue light in Arch3-expressing mice is similarly without impact on either mode of secretion.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in the current manuscript.

claim: Switching to the incorrect wavelength blue light in Arch3-expressing mice is without impact on either LH pulse or surge secretion.
source: We have also performed both yellow and blue light laser controls in these studies and show that the activating yellow light has no impact on LH pulses or the LH surge in wild-type mice and that switching to the incorrect wavelength blue light in Arch3-expressing mice is similarly without impact on either mode of secretion.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in the current manuscript.

claim: The majority of hypophysiotropic GnRH neurons in the rPOA express cFos at the time of the GnRH/LH surge.
source: The majority of hypophysiotropic GnRH neurons in the rPOA express cFos at the time of the GnRH/LH surge (Hoffman et al., 1993) and evidence suggests that neighboring kisspeptin neurons provide a key stimulatory synaptic input to the GnRH neuron at this time (for review see Herbison, 2016; Moenter et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Neighboring kisspeptin neurons provide a key stimulatory synaptic input to the GnRH neuron at the time of the LH surge.
source: The majority of hypophysiotropic GnRH neurons in the rPOA express cFos at the time of the GnRH/LH surge (Hoffman et al., 1993) and evidence suggests that neighboring kisspeptin neurons provide a key stimulatory synaptic input to the GnRH neuron at this time (for review see Herbison, 2016; Moenter et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The overall pattern of GnRH neuron firing may be more important than any average firing rate for surge induction.
source: It is notable that the optogenetic activation of archaerhodopsin-3 does not completely suppress firing but entrains a 10 s on 10 s off pattern of firing every 30 min. As this was effective in stopping the surge, this suggests that the overall pattern of GnRH neuron firing may be more important than any average firing rate for surge induction.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Action potential transmission to the GnRH terminals and/or further synaptic integration at the distal dendritic zone is necessary for the surge.
source: We also note that the chemogenetic inhibition of the distal GnRH projections was effective in blocking the LH surge indicating that action potential transmission to the GnRH terminals and/or further synaptic integration at the distal dendritic zone is necessary for the surge.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: GABA, glutamate and kisspeptin are all active in regulating the activity of the GnRH neuron distal dendron.
source: Studies in the brain slice indicate that GABA, glutamate and kisspeptin are all active in regulating the activity of the GnRH neuron distal dendron (Herde et al., 2013; Iremonger et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: It seems very likely that the arcuate nucleus (ARN) kisspeptin neurons target the distal dendritic zone to generate pulsatile GnRH/LH secretion.
source: Furthermore, it seems very likely that the arcuate nucleus (ARN) kisspeptin neurons target this dendritic zone to generate pulsatile GnRH/LH secretion (Herbison, 2018; Plant, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature and represents an inference based on existing knowledge.

claim: There is very little evidence that the intrinsic properties of adult GnRH neurons contribute to the generation of LH pulses.
source: However, it seems very likely that the suppression of episodic GnRH secretion results from alterations in synaptic integration; first, there is very little evidence that the intrinsic properties of adult GnRH neurons contribute to the generation of LH pulses (Herbison, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: There is robust evidence in several species for the kisspeptin neuron pulse generator to operate synaptically to drive LH pulses.
source: Second, we show here that there is substantial synaptic density at the dendron and third, there is robust evidence in several species for the kisspeptin neuron pulse generator to operate synaptically to drive LH pulses (Herbison, 2018; Moore et al., 2018a; Plant, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The local chemogenetic inhibition of distal GnRH neuron projections in and around the median eminence exerts a very substantial suppression of pulsatile LH release but it does not stop entirely.
source: We find here that the local chemogenetic inhibition of distal GnRH neuron projections in and around the median eminence exerts a very substantial suppression of pulsatile LH release but it does not stop entirely.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The same result was observed with chemogenetic inhibition of the entire GnRH neuron as with local inhibition of distal projections.
source: Notably, the same result was observed with chemogenetic inhibition of the entire GnRH neuron.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: CNO activation of Gi signalling within GnRH distal projections may be insufficient to arrest completely the potent Gq/11-mediated effects of kisspeptin on both TRPC and voltage-gated calcium channels in the dendron.
source: This may result from the CNO activation of Gi signalling within GnRH distal projections being insufficient to arrest completely the potent Gq/11-mediated effects of kisspeptin on both TRPC and voltage-gated calcium channels in the dendron (Iremonger et al., 2017; Smith et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data, supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The soma and proximal dendritic compartments of rPOA GnRH neurons are not required for the generation of LH pulses.
source: Neither chemogenetic nor optogenetic inhibition of rPOA GnRH neuron soma and dendrites had any effect on pulsatile LH secretion despite abolishing the LH surge. This demonstrates that the soma and proximal dendritic compartments of rPOA GnRH neurons are not required for the generation of LH pulses.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The action potential initiation zones for GnRH neurons are only located in the proximal regions.
source: As the action potential initiation zones for GnRH neurons are only located in these proximal regions (Herde and Herbison, 2015; Herde et al., 2013), this suggests that the propagation of action potentials down the dendron are not required for pulsatile secretion.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The propagation of action potentials down the dendron are not required for pulsatile secretion.
source: As the action potential initiation zones for GnRH neurons are only located in these proximal regions (Herde and Herbison, 2015; Herde et al., 2013), this suggests that the propagation of action potentials down the dendron are not required for pulsatile secretion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and prior knowledge.

claim: Episodic GnRH secretion can occur in in vitro preparations without GnRH cell bodies.
source: This is compatible with the demonstration of episodic GnRH secretion in in vitro preparations without GnRH cell bodies (Purnelle et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Reducing the number of hypophysiotropic GnRH neurons has a marked effect on LH pulse amplitude.
source: However, this seems unlikely as reducing the number of hypophysiotropic GnRH neurons has a marked effect on LH pulse amplitude (Czieselsky et al., 2016) and we saw no change in LH pulse amplitude following either inhibition strategy.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The pulse generator is formed by ARN kisspeptin neurons that are intermittently synchronized and send excitatory projections to the GnRH neuron distal dendron in the mouse.
source: It has recently become clear that the pulse generator is formed by ARN kisspeptin neurons that are intermittently synchronized and send excitatory projections to the GnRH neuron distal dendron in the mouse (Clarkson et al., 2017; Herbison, 2018; Moore et al., 2018a; Plant, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Kisspeptin activation of the GnRH neuron distal dendrons and consequent GnRH secretion in the ME has repeatedly been shown to occur in the absence of action potential generation.
source: This kisspeptin activation of the GnRH neuron distal dendrons and consequent GnRH secretion in the ME has repeatedly been shown to occur in the absence of action potential generation (d'Anglemont de Tassigny et al., 2008; Glanowska and Moenter, 2015; Iremonger et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The synaptic innervation of the distal dendron represents a highly localized, autonomous regulatory mechanism for the generation of pulsatile GnRH/LH secretion.
source: As such, it seems highly likely that the synaptic innervation of the distal dendron represents a highly localized, autonomous regulatory mechanism for the generation of pulsatile GnRH/LH secretion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and prior knowledge.

claim: The present observations provide the first in vivo evidence in support of the concept that the distal dendron is an autonomous regulatory mechanism for pulsatile GnRH secretion.
source: The present observations provide the first in vivo evidence in support of this concept and demonstrate a novel mechanism for the synchronization of neural output within the forebrain.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The unique embryonic migration of the GnRH neurons from the nose into the brain results in their somata being scattered throughout the basal forebrain but their projections being concentrated together just above the ME.
source: It is possible that this unusual situation arises from the unique embryonic migration of the GnRH neurons from the nose into the brain resulting in their somata being scattered throughout the basal forebrain but their projections being concentrated together just above the ME (Wray, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The robust synaptic innervation of clustered distal dendronic projections likely provides an efficient solution for the afferent synchronization of an otherwise widely dispersed neural population.
source: The robust synaptic innervation of these clustered distal dendronic projections likely provides an efficient solution for the afferent synchronization of an otherwise widely dispersed neural population.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and prior knowledge.

claim: Expansion microscopy operates on the principal of isotropic swelling of the tissue specimen (typically by 4–5 times) before undertaking regular confocal microscopy.
source: Expansion microscopy operates on the principal of isotropic swelling of the tissue specimen (typically by 4–5 times) before undertaking regular confocal microscopy; thereby providing ~70 nm resolution in brain tissue (Wassie et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Expansion microscopy provides ~70 nm resolution in brain tissue.
source: Expansion microscopy operates on the principal of isotropic swelling of the tissue specimen (typically by 4–5 times) before undertaking regular confocal microscopy; thereby providing ~70 nm resolution in brain tissue (Wassie et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The overlap between cytoplasmic GFP and the presynaptic marker VGAT must be >0.23 μm (0.95 μm post-expansion) to represent a synapse.
source: This revealed that the overlap between cytoplasmic GFP and the presynaptic marker VGAT must be >0.23 μm (0.95 μm post-expansion) to represent a synapse; the gephyrin signal was contained within the GFP signal and all 25 synapses had an overlap in VGAT and GFP signals > 0.23 μm (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on analysis of expansion microscopy data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Synapses in the 'face view' orientation have >0.42 μm (1.75 μm post-expansion) overlap in VGAT and GFP signals in the z-axis.
